summary:
GeoRain is an offline-ready Progressive Web Application (PWA) designed to support landslide preparedness in mountainous and hilly areas, particularly in regions with limited internet connectivity. The application integrates NASA Earth observation data to monitor environmental factors associated with landslide risks, including rainfall, soil moisture, terrain conditions, and changes in forest cover and vegetation.

GeoRain provides an environmental monitoring dashboard, rainfall information, interactive landslide risk maps, risk scenario simulations, evacuation guidance, and an AI-powered educational assistant. Through its offline-first approach, essential application resources, previously cached environmental information, and safety guidance can remain accessible without an active internet connection. Data can be refreshed and synchronized when connectivity becomes available again. GeoRain aims to make satellite-based environmental information more accessible and help communities improve disaster awareness and preparedness.
details:
How It Works

GeoRain is an offline-ready Progressive Web Application (PWA) designed to support landslide early warning and disaster preparedness in mountainous and hilly areas. It evaluates landslide risk through two main components: weather triggers and land vulnerability.

Weather triggers consider rainfall and soil moisture, while land vulnerability considers slope conditions, forest cover, vegetation, and geological factors. The application presents environmental monitoring information, a 14-day rainfall overview, landslide risk indicators, and interactive risk scenario simulations, allowing users to explore how additional rainfall may influence potential risk levels.

GeoRain also provides hazard zone maps, evacuation location guidance, and an AI-powered educational assistant to help users understand landslide preparedness. Its PWA architecture allows users to install the application and access cached essential information when an internet connection is unavailable. Data updates and online services require connectivity.

Benefits and Intended Impact

GeoRain aims to make landslide risk information more accessible, particularly for communities living in mountainous areas where internet connectivity may be limited. By combining environmental indicators and geographical information, it helps users understand factors that may contribute to landslides, recognize potentially vulnerable areas, and prepare appropriate preventive actions.

The intended impact is to increase public awareness, encourage early preparedness, support informed evacuation decisions, and reduce the potential impact of landslide disasters on vulnerable communities.

Tools, Technologies, and Data

GeoRain is developed as a Progressive Web Application (PWA) and deployed through Netlify. Its concept incorporates NASA Earth observation datasets and environmental indicators, including:

  • NASA GPM IMERG for satellite-based rainfall monitoring.
  • NASA SRTM for elevation and terrain slope analysis.
  • Satellite-based forest cover and vegetation information for monitoring environmental changes.

The project also incorporates geographical visualization, offline-accessible application resources, risk scenario simulations, and AI-assisted disaster education.

Creativity and Innovation

GeoRain goes beyond conventional rainfall monitoring by considering both natural triggers and land vulnerability, including changes in forest cover and vegetation that may be associated with human activities such as deforestation and land conversion.

Its main innovation is combining satellite-based environmental awareness, geographical risk information, interactive scenario simulations, and offline accessibility into one community-oriented application. Rather than simply displaying hazard information, GeoRain encourages users to understand environmental conditions and take preventive measures.

Factors Considered

The project considers several important factors: geographical conditions in mountainous areas, rainfall intensity, soil moisture, slope characteristics, forest cover changes, vegetation conditions, geological vulnerability, internet accessibility, and community safety.

Particular attention is given to communities in remote areas that may experience limited connectivity and have difficulty accessing timely disaster information. GeoRain is designed to make essential preparedness information more accessible while emphasizing that its risk scores are educational estimates, not official disaster warnings.
